Consult Summary:
- 48-year-old man with 3-day history of acute watery diarrhoea (5–6 times/day) that began after brief self-limited vomiting; no blood, no abdominal pain; feels dehydrated and weak. Impression: viral/bacterial gastroenteritis. Advised oral rehydration (Dioralyte), symptomatic care, time off work, and review if not improving within one week.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Acute diarrhoea.
- Onset/duration: Started 3 days ago with 2 episodes of vomiting; vomiting has resolved; diarrhoea persists.
- Character: Watery, loose stools, ~5–6 times daily.
- Associated symptoms: Early mild fever (now resolved), weakness, reduced appetite, subjective dehydration (“can’t drink enough”). Denies abdominal pain, blood in stool, headache, or myalgia.
- Triggers/exposures: No recalled takeaway or “dodgy” food; no known sick contacts.
- Systems review: Negative for abdominal pain, rectal bleeding, headache, muscle pain; positive for weakness and reduced oral intake.

Past Medical History:
- Asthma – uses short-acting bronchodilator inhaler as needed; no recent exacerbations reported.

Medications:
- Blue inhaler (short-acting bronchodilator) – dose/route/frequency not documented.
Allergies:
- No known drug allergies.

Social History:
- Lives alone.
- Occupation: Software engineer; off work for past 3 days due to illness.
- Smoking: Denies.
- Alcohol: Occasional/social.
- Recreational drugs: Not mentioned.

Family History:
- Father: Hypertension; died of bowel cancer at ~age unspecified (10 years ago).
- Mother: Type 2 diabetes.
- No other familial conditions mentioned.

Physical Examination:
- Not performed / not documented (no vitals provided).

Investigations:
- None ordered or reported.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Acute gastroenteritis with dehydration risk
  - Assessment: 3-day watery diarrhoea; likely viral/bacterial gastroenteritis; mild dehydration symptoms, no red-flag features (no blood, no severe pain, vomiting resolved).
  - Plan:
    • Oral rehydration therapy: purchase and use Dioralyte or equivalent ORS solution.  
    • Encourage liberal clear fluids; small frequent sips if large volumes not tolerated.  
    • Paracetamol as needed for fever or malaise (dose not specified).  
    • Dietary advice: light diet as tolerated; avoid dairy/caffeine/alcohol until recovery.  
    • Time off work until symptom-free for 24–48 h.  
    • Safety-net: return/seek review if symptoms worsen, bloody stool, persistent vomiting, high fever, or no improvement within one week.

Issue 2: Asthma (stable)
  - Assessment: Intermittent use of reliever inhaler; no current respiratory complaints.
  - Plan:
    • Continue inhaler as required.  
    • No change in asthma management indicated.

General Plan items:
  - Follow-up: Re-consult next week if diarrhoea not resolved or earlier for red-flag symptoms.
  - Documentation of hydration status and vitals recommended at next contact if symptoms persist.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing but clinically expected: vitals, physical examination, medication list reconciliation (other OTC, supplements), allergy confirmation to non-drug substances, past surgical history, immunisation status.
● Internal conflicts: None noted.
● Transcript quality: Clear audio; minor filler words, no significant inaudible sections.
